text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Toronto softens smoking law: Restaurant, bar patrons can light up in designated areas with new amendments.
- Job bias hits older workers: study: Over-45s given the cold shoulder.
- Rebel strike shuts down Kinshasa: Zairian protest called by Tshisekedi's supporters aim at forcing Mobutu's ouster.
- Mulroney wants unity back on front burner: Former PM urges leaders to try to return Quebec to fold.
- Canada tempers line on rights in China: Ottawa won't sign UN resolution.
- Daimler buys into Ballard: B.C. fuel-cell maker in C$508-million alliance with German transportation giant.
- Repap buys time by striking deal with banks: Lenders' support allows firm to seek sale of mills, company.
- GM Canada fights to reclaim market share: Boosts financing, marketing, and advertising.
- New Busang samples head for testing: Four labs to estimate amount of gold.
- Benz backs Ballard in electric car deal: German auto giant takes 25 percent stake in Canadian fuel-cell firm as part of C$510-million venture to build pollution-free vehicles.
- Repap ready to sell company piecemeal.
